name: The system acts on time
principle: Standing work happens when it is due, in the person's own time, or when something happens that calls for it, without anyone having to ask.
state_description: Each schedule runs once per period, a requested run runs, an event runs a reactive schedule, and a corrupt time never stops one.
hints_of_measurement: Schedules due against schedules that should be due, over the cadence, zone, request and event cases.

name: Recurring work keeps its days and times
principle: Recurring work starts on the days and at the time of day its person keeps, in their own time zone, once per occasion, and a start that is a little late still counts.
state_description: A schedule with days, a time of day, a time zone and a grace window is due once in each occasion, from the moment it arrives until the grace window ends, whatever the daylight-saving changes, and not on other days.
hints_of_measurement: Schedules due against schedules that should be due, over the day, time, time zone, grace and daylight-saving cases.

name: Standing work changes something outside itself
principle: Each run of standing work changes something outside itself that its own acts can move within days, and leaves the next step ordered for the next run.
state_description: The standing instructions meet the eight points of the standing work standard, and the metric of the work moves in most of its recent real runs through the run's own acts.
hints_of_measurement: The share of the eight points the standing instructions meet, then the share of recent real runs whose metric moved.
